meta.title: Style preview: synthetic fixture, not a real audit
meta.summary: This is a fixture, not an audit. Every score, finding and quote below is invented to exercise the report template: five severity levels, all four verdicts, a scored and an unscored dimension, and one dimension in each score band. Use it to preview styling changes without re-running a real audit.
assumptions: Screens are placeholders generated by fixtures/make_placeholders.py, not a real product.
limitations: Nothing here was measured. The numbers are chosen to land one dimension in each colour band.

signals: status bar and tab bar blocks present

scorecard.standard: System status is visible: the screen says what state it is in
scorecard.reasoning: Fixture row: rendered as a pass so the green verdict dot appears in this table.

scorecard.standard: Language matches the audience rather than the system
Icons are recognisable without labels, or are labelled
scorecard.reasoning: Fixture row: rendered as a partial so the orange verdict dot appears.

scorecard.standard: Type scale holds a consistent ratio across levels
Primary action is the most visually prominent control
scorecard.reasoning: Fixture row: rendered as a fail so the red verdict dot appears and Visual design lands in the red band.

scorecard.standard: Text contrast meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text)
Measured text spacing leaves room for user overrides
Every control exposes a programmatic name, role and value
scorecard.naReason: Needs the DOM or a Figma file; a screenshot carries no accessibility tree.

scorecard.standard: Colour values resolve to a shared token set
scorecard.naReason: Token checks need the source file; this fixture ships images only.

scorecard.standard: Spacing steps come from one scale
scorecard.naReason: Same as CO-03. This is what an entirely unscored dimension looks like.

scorecard.standard: Each step states what happens next
The user can reverse a step without losing entered data
scorecard.reasoning: Fixture row: both UF rows pass so User flow lands at 100.

findings.title: Critical: the highest severity, rendered in red
findings.evidence: Fixture finding pinned to the primary-action block. Exists so the red tag, red marker and red card tint are all visible in one place.
findings.fix: Nothing to fix here; this is a fixture. Real findings name a direction and the principle they restore.

findings.title: Major: shares the red hue with Critical
findings.evidence: Pinned to the first content card. Major and Critical deliberately share one red: both mean fix this.

findings.title: Minor: orange, drawn as a region rather than a point
findings.evidence: Carries w and h, so the template renders a dashed region box over the hero block instead of a bare marker.

findings.title: Cosmetic: purple
findings.evidence: Pinned to the second form field on screen 2, so the multi-screen rendering path gets exercised too.

findings.title: Note: blue, the same hue as the watch list
findings.evidence: Lowest severity. Blue is shared with the designer watch list because both mean no score impact.

advisories.title: This is what a watch-list card looks like
advisories.note: Advisories are the channel for things worth a designer's attention that should not move the score: deliberate patterns, audience-dependent calls, and judgements that need context the audit does not have.

advisories.title: A second card, to check vertical rhythm
advisories.note: Two cards make it obvious whether spacing between watch-list entries matches spacing between Areas to Fix entries.

observed: screen-01 → screen-02: the primary action opens the form.
screen-02 → submit: the form ends in a single submit control.
missing: No error state was captured for the form on screen-02.
